---
title: "01_season_screen"
output: html_document
---

Purpose: a fast, frequentist screen of whether the subadult - adult difference in *Bd* infection
changes through the season, before investing in a Bayesian seasonal model. This script fits
`glmmTMB` mixed models per species; it does not produce inferential results for the manuscript.

Questions this screen answers:

1. Which species have enough co-sampling (both life stages sampled in the same weeks) to
   estimate a stage x season interaction at all?
2. Is season confounded with site (populations visited at different times of year) or does
   sampling timing shift between years? Either would blur or fake a seasonal pattern.
3. Does a stage x season interaction improve the fit, once population and population-year
   variation are accounted for, and does it survive adding (pooled) weather?

Why the interaction is the target: weather effects in the unified and GAM models do not vary by
life stage, so weather (and its confounding with season) affects both stages equally and cancels
out of the subadult - adult contrast. The same logic applies to season here: the seasonal curve
shared by both stages may mix true seasonality with weather, but the *difference* between stages
through the season (the interaction) is what this screen is about.

Run order: needs the unified model data from `size_bd_unified/01_model_data.Rmd`
(the same file model m11g was fit to).

# Setup

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| output: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Show setup code"

librarian::shelf(tidyverse, here, glmmTMB)

figures_dir = here("size_bd_season", "figures")
intermediates_dir = here("size_bd_season", "intermediates")
dir.create(figures_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(intermediates_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# unified model data (subadults and adults only, all species)
load(here("size_bd_unified", "intermediates", "bd_model_env_unified_2026-11-12.RData"))

```

# Screen parameters
```{r}
# a week counts as "co-sampled" for prevalence when both life stages have >= min_n_co swabs,
# and for load when both have >= min_pos_co Bd-positive swabs
min_n_co = 5
min_pos_co = 3

# species tiers, from the number of co-sampled weeks:
#   tier 1: prevalence and load screens (enough co-sampled weeks for both)
#   tier 2: prevalence screen only
# (10 / 6 adds anaxyrus canorus and colostethus panamansis to the five ranids)
tier1_min_co_weeks = 10
tier1_min_co_weeks_pos = 6
tier2_min_co_weeks = 7

stage_colors = c(adult = "#0072B2", subadult = "#E69F00")

```

# Season terms
```{r}
# day of year as a first harmonic (one sine + one cosine). together, a * sin + b * cos is a
# single smooth wave with a fitted amplitude and peak date, so two coefficients describe a full
# seasonal cycle. for species sampled only part of the year (e.g. sierra lakes, ~4-6 months),
# the full cycle is not identifiable: within the sampled window the wave acts as a smooth
# within-season trend (rising, falling, or humped), which is fine for a screen but should not be
# read as the shape of the full year.
season_data = brms_data %>%
  mutate(life_stage_simple = factor(life_stage_simple, levels = c("adult", "subadult")),
         doy = yday(date),
         week = pmin(ceiling(doy / 7), 52),
         s1 = sin(2 * pi * doy / 365.25),
         c1 = cos(2 * pi * doy / 365.25),
         # glmmTMB random-effect grouping needs factors; pop_year mirrors the unified model's
         # population:year grouping
         population = factor(population),
         pop_year = interaction(population, year, drop = TRUE),
         log_load = if_else(bd_detected_co100, log(bd_load_co100_density), NA_real_))

```

# Coverage and species tiers
```{r}
# weeks where both life stages were sampled (prevalence) or both had positives (load)
co_weeks = season_data %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture, week, life_stage_simple) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            n_pos = sum(bd_detected_co100),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = life_stage_simple, values_from = c(n, n_pos), values_fill = 0) %>%
  mutate(co_prev = n_adult >= min_n_co & n_subadult >= min_n_co,
         co_load = n_pos_adult >= min_pos_co & n_pos_subadult >= min_pos_co)

coverage = season_data %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            years = n_distinct(year),
            visits = n_distinct(paste(site, date)),
            weeks = n_distinct(week),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(co_weeks %>%
              group_by(taxon_capture) %>%
              summarise(co_weeks = sum(co_prev),
                        co_weeks_pos = sum(co_load),
                        .groups = "drop"),
            by = "taxon_capture") %>%
  mutate(tier = case_when(co_weeks >= tier1_min_co_weeks & co_weeks_pos >= tier1_min_co_weeks_pos ~ 1,
                          co_weeks >= tier2_min_co_weeks ~ 2,
                          .default = 3)) %>%
  arrange(tier, desc(co_weeks))

coverage

tier1_spp = coverage %>% filter(tier == 1) %>% pull(taxon_capture)
tier2_spp = coverage %>% filter(tier == 2) %>% pull(taxon_capture)

```

# Design checks

## Season vs site
```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 10

# rows are populations, columns weeks, fill is the number of swabs. if different populations
# are sampled at different times of year (e.g. high-elevation lakes late in summer), then
# "season" partly means "site", and a stage x season interaction could reflect which sites
# carry which life stages. the population random effect absorbs site-level differences in
# average infection, but not site-specific seasonal patterns.
p_pop_week = season_data %>%
  filter(taxon_capture %in% tier1_spp) %>%
  count(taxon_capture, population, week) %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture) %>%
  # order populations by their median sampling week, so timing differences show as a diagonal
  mutate(population = fct_reorder(population, week, .fun = median)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = week, y = population, fill = n)) +
  geom_tile() +
  facet_wrap(~ taxon_capture, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10") +
  labs(x = "Week of year", y = "Population (ordered by median sampling week)", fill = "Swabs") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank())

ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "01_population_week_sampling.png"), p_pop_week, width = 12, height = 10)

p_pop_week

```

## Timing between years
```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 8

# sampling dates by year and life stage (median and interquartile range of day of year). if
# subadult timing shifts a lot between years, pooling years by day of year blurs seasonal
# patterns; population-year random effects absorb year-level shifts in average infection, not
# shifts in timing.
p_year_timing = season_data %>%
  filter(taxon_capture %in% tier1_spp) %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture, year, life_stage_simple) %>%
  summarise(doy_median = median(doy),
            doy_q25 = quantile(doy, 0.25),
            doy_q75 = quantile(doy, 0.75),
            n = n(),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = doy_median, color = life_stage_simple)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = doy_q25, ymax = doy_q75, size = n),
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(0.1, 0.8), trans = "sqrt") +
  facet_wrap(~ taxon_capture, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Day of year sampled (median, IQR)", color = "Life stage", size = "Swabs") +
  theme_minimal()

ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "01_year_sampling_timing.png"), p_year_timing, width = 12, height = 8)

p_year_timing

```

# Mixed-model screen
```{r}
# for each species and response, compare a model without and with the stage x season
# interaction, using a likelihood-ratio test (LRT) and the change in AIC:
#   m0: response ~ life_stage + s1 + c1                      (one seasonal curve, shifted by stage)
#   m1: response ~ life_stage * (s1 + c1)                    (separate seasonal curve per stage)
# both with (1 | population) + (1 | pop_year). the weather variant adds pooled (within-species,
# not stage-specific) temp_c_30_z + precip_mm_10_z to both models. this adjusts the shared
# seasonal curve for weather, but a weather effect common to both stages cannot create or remove
# a difference between stages, so the interaction is rarely changed much by it. whether the
# interaction could instead be stage-specific weather sensitivity is tested in the separability
# section below.
#
# responses:
#   prevalence: bd_detected_co100, binomial (logit link), all swabs
#   load: log(bd load density), gaussian, bd-positive swabs only (the hurdle model's mu part)
#
# caveats:
#   - random intercepts only. the unified model also lets population effects differ by life
#     stage, (life_stage | pop_year); adding that here is possible but often fails to converge
#     with these data sizes. without it, LRT p-values may be somewhat optimistic.
#   - p-values from many species x response x variant tests are a screen, not a result; look
#     for consistent, large effects (and the contrast curves below), not p < 0.05.

fit_screen = function(d, response, family, weather) {
  rhs_0 = "life_stage_simple + s1 + c1"
  rhs_1 = "life_stage_simple * (s1 + c1)"
  rhs_weather = if (weather) " + temp_c_30_z + precip_mm_10_z" else ""
  rhs_re = " + (1 | population) + (1 | pop_year)"

  f0 = as.formula(paste(response, "~", rhs_0, rhs_weather, rhs_re))
  f1 = as.formula(paste(response, "~", rhs_1, rhs_weather, rhs_re))

  # tryCatch keeps the loop going if one species fails to fit
  m0 = tryCatch(glmmTMB(f0, data = d, family = family), error = function(e) NULL)
  m1 = tryCatch(glmmTMB(f1, data = d, family = family), error = function(e) NULL)

  if (is.null(m0) || is.null(m1)) {
    return(tibble(converged = FALSE, lrt_p = NA_real_, delta_aic = NA_real_, fit_1 = list(m1)))
  }

  # pdHess = FALSE means the optimizer did not reach a well-defined optimum; treat with caution
  converged = isTRUE(m0$sdr$pdHess) && isTRUE(m1$sdr$pdHess)
  lrt = anova(m0, m1)

  tibble(converged = converged,
         lrt_p = lrt$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2],
         delta_aic = AIC(m1) - AIC(m0),   # negative favors the interaction model
         fit_1 = list(m1))
}

# one row per species x response x weather variant. tier 1: prevalence and load; tier 2:
# prevalence only
screen_grid = bind_rows(
  expand_grid(taxon_capture = c(tier1_spp, tier2_spp), metric = "prevalence"),
  expand_grid(taxon_capture = tier1_spp, metric = "load")) %>%
  expand_grid(weather = c(FALSE, TRUE))

screen_results = screen_grid %>%
  mutate(fit = pmap(list(taxon_capture, metric, weather), function(spp, met, wx) {
    d = season_data %>% filter(taxon_capture == spp)

    if (met == "prevalence") {
      fit_screen(d, "bd_detected_co100", binomial(), wx)
    } else {
      fit_screen(filter(d, bd_detected_co100), "log_load", gaussian(), wx)
    }
  })) %>%
  unnest(fit)

# summary table (without the fitted models)
screen_table = screen_results %>%
  select(-fit_1) %>%
  arrange(metric, taxon_capture, weather)

write_csv(screen_table, file.path(intermediates_dir, "01_season_screen_lrt.csv"))

screen_table

```

# Contrast curves
```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 9

# subadult - adult contrast through the season from the interaction model (m1):
#   contrast(doy) = b_subadult + b_subadult:s1 * sin(doy) + b_subadult:c1 * cos(doy)
# on the logit scale (log odds ratio of detection) or log scale (log fold difference in load).
# its standard error comes from the fixed-effect covariance matrix V: for the row vector
# L = (1, sin, cos), var(contrast) = L V L'. intervals are approximate (wald, 95%).
# curves are shown only at weeks where both stages were sampled (co_prev / co_load), so nothing
# is extrapolated into unsampled parts of the season.
contrast_terms = c("life_stage_simplesubadult",
                   "life_stage_simplesubadult:s1",
                   "life_stage_simplesubadult:c1")

contrast_curve = function(fit, weeks) {
  b = fixef(fit)$cond
  V = vcov(fit)$cond
  stopifnot(all(contrast_terms %in% names(b)))

  doy = weeks * 7 - 3   # mid-week day of year
  L = cbind(1, sin(2 * pi * doy / 365.25), cos(2 * pi * doy / 365.25))

  est = as.vector(L %*% b[contrast_terms])
  se = sqrt(diag(L %*% V[contrast_terms, contrast_terms] %*% t(L)))

  tibble(week = weeks, contrast = est, lower = est - 1.96 * se, upper = est + 1.96 * se)
}

contrast_curves = screen_results %>%
  filter(!map_lgl(fit_1, is.null)) %>%
  mutate(curve = pmap(list(fit_1, taxon_capture, metric), function(fit, spp, met) {
    co = co_weeks %>% filter(taxon_capture == spp)
    weeks = if (met == "prevalence") co$week[co$co_prev] else co$week[co$co_load]
    contrast_curve(fit, sort(weeks))
  })) %>%
  select(taxon_capture, metric, weather, converged, curve) %>%
  unnest(curve)

write_csv(contrast_curves, file.path(intermediates_dir, "01_season_contrast_curves.csv"))

plot_contrast = function(met, y_label) {
  contrast_curves %>%
    filter(metric == met) %>%
    mutate(weather = if_else(weather, "with weather", "season only")) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = week, y = contrast, color = weather)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#555") +
    geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), size = 0.2,
                    position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
    facet_wrap(~ taxon_capture, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(x = "Week of year (co-sampled weeks only)", y = y_label, color = NULL) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}

p_contrast_prev = plot_contrast("prevalence", "Subadult - adult log odds ratio of detection")
p_contrast_load = plot_contrast("load", "Subadult - adult log fold difference in Bd load density (positives)")

ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "01_season_contrast_prevalence.png"), p_contrast_prev, width = 12, height = 9)
ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "01_season_contrast_load.png"), p_contrast_load, width = 12, height = 7)

p_contrast_prev
p_contrast_load

```

# Size class curves
```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 9

# seasonal curve for each life stage from the interaction model (m1), alongside observed weekly
# values. the curves are fixed-effect predictions for a typical population and year (random
# effects at 0):
#   adult:    b0 + b_s1 * sin + b_c1 * cos [+ weather terms]
#   subadult: adult + b_subadult + b_subadult:s1 * sin + b_subadult:c1 * cos
# so the vertical gap between the two curves at any week is the contrast plotted above.
# prevalence curves are back-transformed from the logit scale (inverse logit); load curves stay
# on the log scale. intervals are approximate wald 95% intervals (L V L', as for the contrasts),
# transformed with the curve.
#
# each stage's curve is drawn only at weeks where that stage was sampled (>= min_n_co swabs for
# prevalence, >= min_pos_co positives for load), and lines break across unsampled weeks.
# levels are within-species only: never compare curve heights between species.
#
# curve_weather: which screen variant to plot. FALSE = season only. TRUE = with weather, holding
# temp_c_30_z and precip_mm_10_z at the species' median (so the curve shows season at typical
# weather for that species, not the dataset-wide mean).
curve_weather = FALSE

# species-median weather (on the model's z scale), used only when curve_weather = TRUE
spp_weather = season_data %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture) %>%
  summarise(temp_c_30_z = median(temp_c_30_z),
            precip_mm_10_z = median(precip_mm_10_z),
            .groups = "drop")

stage_curves = function(fit, weeks_adult, weeks_subadult, weather_values) {
  b = fixef(fit)$cond
  V = vcov(fit)$cond

  grid = bind_rows(tibble(life_stage_simple = "adult", week = weeks_adult),
                   tibble(life_stage_simple = "subadult", week = weeks_subadult)) %>%
    mutate(doy = week * 7 - 3,   # mid-week day of year
           s1 = sin(2 * pi * doy / 365.25),
           c1 = cos(2 * pi * doy / 365.25),
           is_sub = as.numeric(life_stage_simple == "subadult"))

  # one row of L per stage x week, one column per fixed effect (named as in fixef). any term
  # not set here stays 0
  L = matrix(0, nrow = nrow(grid), ncol = length(b), dimnames = list(NULL, names(b)))
  L[, "(Intercept)"] = 1
  L[, "s1"] = grid$s1
  L[, "c1"] = grid$c1
  L[, "life_stage_simplesubadult"] = grid$is_sub
  L[, "life_stage_simplesubadult:s1"] = grid$is_sub * grid$s1
  L[, "life_stage_simplesubadult:c1"] = grid$is_sub * grid$c1
  for (wx in names(weather_values)) {
    if (wx %in% names(b)) L[, wx] = weather_values[[wx]]
  }

  est = as.vector(L %*% b)
  se = sqrt(rowSums((L %*% V) * L))   # diag(L V L') without building the full matrix

  grid %>%
    mutate(est = est, lower = est - 1.96 * se, upper = est + 1.96 * se) %>%
    select(life_stage_simple, week, est, lower, upper)
}

# observed weekly values per stage: proportion positive (prevalence) and mean log load among
# positives (load), with the counts they are based on
observed_weekly = season_data %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture, week, life_stage_simple) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            n_pos = sum(bd_detected_co100),
            prevalence = n_pos / n,
            load = if (n_pos > 0) mean(log_load, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(life_stage_simple = as.character(life_stage_simple))

curves = screen_results %>%
  filter(weather == curve_weather, !map_lgl(fit_1, is.null)) %>%
  mutate(curve = pmap(list(fit_1, taxon_capture, metric), function(fit, spp, met) {
    obs = observed_weekly %>% filter(taxon_capture == spp)
    if (met == "prevalence") {
      sampled = obs %>% filter(n >= min_n_co)
    } else {
      sampled = obs %>% filter(n_pos >= min_pos_co)
    }
    wx = spp_weather %>% filter(taxon_capture == spp) %>% select(-taxon_capture) %>% as.list()

    stage_curves(fit,
                 weeks_adult = sort(sampled$week[sampled$life_stage_simple == "adult"]),
                 weeks_subadult = sort(sampled$week[sampled$life_stage_simple == "subadult"]),
                 weather_values = wx)
  })) %>%
  select(taxon_capture, metric, converged, curve) %>%
  unnest(curve) %>%
  # back-transform prevalence from the logit scale
  mutate(across(c(est, lower, upper), ~ if_else(metric == "prevalence", plogis(.x), .x))) %>%
  # run id: a new run starts after any gap in sampled weeks, so lines are not drawn across gaps
  group_by(taxon_capture, metric, life_stage_simple) %>%
  arrange(week, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(run = cumsum(c(1, diff(week) > 1))) %>%
  ungroup()

write_csv(curves, file.path(intermediates_dir, "01_season_stage_curves.csv"))

plot_stage_curves = function(met, y_label) {
  obs = observed_weekly %>%
    filter(taxon_capture %in% unique(curves$taxon_capture[curves$metric == met])) %>%
    filter(if (met == "prevalence") n >= min_n_co else n_pos >= min_pos_co) %>%
    mutate(value = if (met == "prevalence") prevalence else load,
           weight = if (met == "prevalence") n else n_pos)

  curves %>%
    filter(metric == met) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = week, color = life_stage_simple, fill = life_stage_simple)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper, group = interaction(life_stage_simple, run)),
                alpha = 0.2, color = NA) +
    geom_line(aes(y = est, group = interaction(life_stage_simple, run)), linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_point(data = obs, aes(y = value, size = weight), alpha = 0.5, shape = 16) +
    facet_wrap(~ taxon_capture, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_color_manual(values = stage_colors) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = stage_colors) +
    scale_size_area(max_size = 3) +
    labs(x = "Week of year", y = y_label, color = "Life stage", fill = "Life stage",
         size = if (met == "prevalence") "Swabs" else "Positives",
         caption = paste0("Lines: interaction-model fit (", if (curve_weather) "with weather at species median" else "season only",
                          "), 95% wald intervals. Points: observed weekly values.")) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}

p_curves_prev = plot_stage_curves("prevalence", "Bd prevalence (typical population and year)")
p_curves_load = plot_stage_curves("load", "Mean log(Bd load density) among positives (typical population and year)")

ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "01_season_stage_curves_prevalence.png"), p_curves_prev, width = 12, height = 9)
ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "01_season_stage_curves_load.png"), p_curves_load, width = 12, height = 7)

p_curves_prev
p_curves_load

```

# Separability of stage x season and stage x weather

Within temperate species, 30-day temperature closely follows the season, so "the subadult -
adult difference changes through the season" (stage x season) and "subadults respond to
temperature differently than adults" (stage x temperature) can produce nearly the same pattern.
This section asks, per tier-1 species, whether the data can tell the two apart.

## Temperature anomalies
```{r}
# split temperature, within each species, into a seasonal part (what the first harmonic of day
# of year predicts) and an anomaly (warmer or colder than usual for that date, e.g. a warm
# summer, or a low-elevation site). the anomaly is uncorrelated with s1 and c1 by construction
# (least-squares residuals), so a stage x temp_anom term does not compete with stage x season.
# the decomposition uses all of a species' swabs; in the positives-only load models the anomaly
# is close to, but not exactly, uncorrelated with season.
#
# caveat: using anomalies assumes a frog responds the same way to "warmer than usual for june"
# as to "june is warmer than may". acclimation could make these differ, and that cannot be
# tested with these data.
season_data = season_data %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture) %>%
  mutate(temp_seasonal = fitted(lm(temp_c_30_z ~ s1 + c1)),
         temp_anom = temp_c_30_z - temp_seasonal) %>%
  ungroup()

# share of within-species temperature variance that is seasonal (high = stage x season and
# stage x temperature are hard to separate)
season_data %>%
  filter(taxon_capture %in% tier1_spp) %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture) %>%
  summarise(temp_seasonal_r2 = var(temp_seasonal) / var(temp_c_30_z),
            temp_anom_sd = sd(temp_anom),
            .groups = "drop")

```

## Competing models
```{r}
# five models per species and response (same random effects as the screen):
#   m_none:    stage + s1 + c1 + temp + precip                (no stage-dependent pattern)
#   m_season:  stage * (s1 + c1) + temp + precip              (stage difference varies by date)
#   m_weather: stage * (temp + precip) + s1 + c1              (stage difference varies by weather)
#   m_both:    stage * (s1 + c1 + temp + precip)              (both)
#   m_anom:    stage * (s1 + c1 + temp_anom) + precip         (both, with temperature anomalies)
# temp = temp_c_30_z, precip = precip_mm_10_z. m_anom leaves out temp_seasonal on purpose:
# within a species it is an exact linear combination of s1 and c1, so it is already in the model.
#
# checks (alpha = screen_alpha):
#   1. aic_season_minus_weather: AIC(m_season) - AIC(m_weather). |gap| > ~4 favors one story
#      (negative favors season); < ~2 means the data fit both equally well
#   2. p_season_given_weather: LRT m_weather vs m_both (does stage x season add to stage x weather?)
#      p_weather_given_season: LRT m_season vs m_both (does stage x weather add to stage x season?)
#      p_season_alone / p_weather_alone: LRT vs m_none (does each improve on its own?)
#   3. max_cor_season_temp: largest |correlation| between the stage:s1 / stage:c1 and the
#      stage:temp estimates in m_both (near 0.9 or more = the model cannot tell them apart);
#      se_ratio_stage_temp: SE of stage:temp in m_both / in m_weather (large = inflated by
#      collinearity)
#   4. anom_est, anom_lower, anom_upper: stage x temp_anom estimate in m_anom, with a wald 95%
#      interval (logit scale for prevalence, log scale for load)
screen_alpha = 0.05

fit_glmm = function(d, response, rhs, family) {
  f = as.formula(paste(response, "~", rhs, "+ (1 | population) + (1 | pop_year)"))
  tryCatch(glmmTMB(f, data = d, family = family), error = function(e) NULL)
}

lrt_p = function(small, big) {
  if (is.null(small) || is.null(big)) return(NA_real_)
  anova(small, big)$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2]
}

sep_rhs = c(
  none    = "life_stage_simple + s1 + c1 + temp_c_30_z + precip_mm_10_z",
  season  = "life_stage_simple * (s1 + c1) + temp_c_30_z + precip_mm_10_z",
  weather = "life_stage_simple * (temp_c_30_z + precip_mm_10_z) + s1 + c1",
  both    = "life_stage_simple * (s1 + c1 + temp_c_30_z + precip_mm_10_z)",
  anom    = "life_stage_simple * (s1 + c1 + temp_anom) + precip_mm_10_z")

separability_one = function(d, response, family) {
  # purrr:: prefix: maps::map() (from the maps package) masks purrr::map() when maps is attached
  m = purrr::map(sep_rhs, ~ fit_glmm(d, response, .x, family))

  converged = all(map_lgl(m, ~ !is.null(.x) && isTRUE(.x$sdr$pdHess)))

  # 3. collinearity diagnostics from m_both (and m_weather for the SE ratio)
  max_cor = NA_real_
  se_ratio = NA_real_
  if (!is.null(m$both) && !is.null(m$weather)) {
    cor_both = cov2cor(vcov(m$both)$cond)
    season_terms = c("life_stage_simplesubadult:s1", "life_stage_simplesubadult:c1")
    temp_term = "life_stage_simplesubadult:temp_c_30_z"
    max_cor = max(abs(cor_both[season_terms, temp_term]))
    se_ratio = sqrt(vcov(m$both)$cond[temp_term, temp_term]) /
      sqrt(vcov(m$weather)$cond[temp_term, temp_term])
  }

  # 4. stage x temperature anomaly
  anom = tibble(anom_est = NA_real_, anom_lower = NA_real_, anom_upper = NA_real_)
  if (!is.null(m$anom)) {
    anom_term = "life_stage_simplesubadult:temp_anom"
    est = fixef(m$anom)$cond[anom_term]
    se = sqrt(vcov(m$anom)$cond[anom_term, anom_term])
    anom = tibble(anom_est = est, anom_lower = est - 1.96 * se, anom_upper = est + 1.96 * se)
  }

  tibble(converged = converged,
         aic_season_minus_weather = if (is.null(m$season) || is.null(m$weather)) NA_real_ else
           AIC(m$season) - AIC(m$weather),
         p_season_given_weather = lrt_p(m$weather, m$both),
         p_weather_given_season = lrt_p(m$season, m$both),
         p_season_alone = lrt_p(m$none, m$season),
         p_weather_alone = lrt_p(m$none, m$weather),
         max_cor_season_temp = max_cor,
         se_ratio_stage_temp = se_ratio) %>%
    bind_cols(anom)
}

separability = expand_grid(taxon_capture = tier1_spp,
                           metric = c("prevalence", "load")) %>%
  mutate(res = map2(taxon_capture, metric, function(spp, met) {
    d = season_data %>% filter(taxon_capture == spp)
    if (met == "prevalence") {
      separability_one(d, "bd_detected_co100", binomial())
    } else {
      separability_one(filter(d, bd_detected_co100), "log_load", gaussian())
    }
  })) %>%
  unnest(res) %>%
  # reading, following the decision table:
  #   - each adds to the other: separable, both contribute
  #   - only one adds to the other: that story is preferred
  #   - neither adds to the other, but at least one improves on m_none alone: not separable
  #     (the two terms carry the same information)
  #   - neither improves on m_none: no stage-dependent seasonal or weather pattern
  mutate(reading = case_when(
    p_season_given_weather < screen_alpha & p_weather_given_season < screen_alpha ~ "separable: both contribute",
    p_season_given_weather < screen_alpha ~ "seasonal (not weather sensitivity)",
    p_weather_given_season < screen_alpha ~ "weather sensitivity",
    p_season_alone < screen_alpha | p_weather_alone < screen_alpha ~ "not separable",
    !is.na(p_season_alone) ~ "no stage-dependent pattern",
    .default = NA_character_)) %>%
  arrange(metric, taxon_capture)

write_csv(separability, file.path(intermediates_dir, "01_season_separability.csv"))

separability
```

# Coverage for an all-species season model

The tiers above pick species for per-species stage curves. The next modeling step aims instead
at every species with both life stages, using one model form that lets the seasonal part of the
stage contrast shrink to a constant when the data cannot support it (a shrinkage difference
smooth, `s(season, by = ordered(stage), bs = "ts")`). Species with narrow or no co-sampling are
then still included: their contrast becomes a constant offset, and the seasonal summary reports
"uninformative" rather than dropping the species.

This section prepares two things for that model, for all species in the unified data:

1. **A seasonal origin per species**, so the season axis is continuous within each species'
   sampled season. Day of year breaks at 1 January, which cuts the Panamanian dry season
   (about December - April) in two. Placing the origin in the middle of each species' longest
   sampling gap fixes this for any species; for temperate species the gap is winter, so their
   axis is barely changed.
2. **A coverage class per species**, describing how much the data can say about the seasonal
   shape of the contrast (not whether the species is included).

## Coverage parameters
```{r}
# a species enters the all-species model with at least min_n_stage swabs of each life stage.
# this is low on purpose: the stage offset can be estimated from few swabs, and the shrinkage
# smooth handles thin seasonal data
min_n_stage = 20

# a week counts as "sampled" (for finding the seasonal gap) with >= min_n_co swabs of either
# stage combined, so a single stray swab does not split a gap
min_n_gap = min_n_co

# coverage classes, from co-sampled weeks (prevalence rule, both stages >= min_n_co swabs):
#   broad:  >= broad_min_co_weeks co-sampled weeks spread over >= broad_min_co_span_weeks weeks
#           of the (re-originated) season: the seasonal shape of the contrast can be estimated
#   narrow: some co-sampled weeks, but fewer or bunched: expect a mostly constant contrast
#   none:   no co-sampled week: the contrast relies on comparing stages sampled at different
#           times, and the seasonal shape is not identifiable (expect full shrinkage)
broad_min_co_weeks = 6
broad_min_co_span_weeks = 8

classify_coverage = function(co_weeks, co_span_weeks) {
  class = case_when(co_weeks >= broad_min_co_weeks & co_span_weeks >= broad_min_co_span_weeks ~ "broad",
                    co_weeks >= 1 ~ "narrow",
                    .default = "none")
  factor(class, levels = c("broad", "narrow", "none"))
}

```

## Seasonal origin
```{r}
# origin week = middle of the longest circular run of unsampled weeks. "circular" because a
# gap can wrap through the new year (e.g. a temperate winter gap spans weeks 45 - 10).
# species sampled in every week (year-round) have no gap; for them the origin is the middle of
# the 4-week window with the fewest swabs.
find_origin_week = function(weekly_n) {
  # weekly_n: swab counts for weeks 1-52 (zeros included)
  sampled = weekly_n >= min_n_gap

  if (all(sampled)) {
    # rolling 4-week sum, wrapping around the year; origin at the window's 2nd-3rd week
    roll = vapply(1:52, function(w) sum(weekly_n[((w - 1):(w + 2)) %% 52 + 1]), numeric(1))
    return(((which.min(roll) + 1) - 1) %% 52 + 1)
  }

  # rotate the year to start at a sampled week, so no gap wraps past the end of the vector,
  # then find the longest run of unsampled weeks with rle() (run-length encoding)
  start = which(sampled)[1]
  idx = c(start:52, seq_len(start - 1))
  runs = rle(sampled[idx])
  run_end = cumsum(runs$lengths)
  run_start = run_end - runs$lengths + 1
  gaps = which(!runs$values)
  longest = gaps[which.max(runs$lengths[gaps])]
  idx[floor((run_start[longest] + run_end[longest]) / 2)]
}

weekly_all = season_data %>%
  count(taxon_capture, life_stage_simple, week) %>%
  complete(taxon_capture, life_stage_simple, week = 1:52, fill = list(n = 0))

season_origin = weekly_all %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture, week) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(taxon_capture, week) %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture) %>%
  summarise(origin_week = find_origin_week(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(origin_doy = origin_week * 7 - 3)   # mid-week day of year

season_origin

```

## Coverage table
```{r}
# week_r: weeks since the species' origin (1 = the origin week). sampled weeks then form one
# continuous block in week_r, even when they straddle the new year
week_since_origin = function(week, origin_week) (week - origin_week) %% 52 + 1

co_weeks_all = co_weeks %>%
  left_join(season_origin, by = "taxon_capture") %>%
  mutate(week_r = week_since_origin(week, origin_week))

coverage_all = season_data %>%
  left_join(season_origin, by = "taxon_capture") %>%
  mutate(week_r = week_since_origin(week, origin_week)) %>%
  group_by(taxon_capture, origin_week) %>%
  summarise(n_adult = sum(life_stage_simple == "adult"),
            n_subadult = sum(life_stage_simple == "subadult"),
            populations = n_distinct(population),
            years = n_distinct(year),
            # central 90% of swabs on the re-originated axis: the sampled season
            season_first_week_r = quantile(week_r, 0.05, type = 1),
            season_last_week_r = quantile(week_r, 0.95, type = 1),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(season_span_weeks = season_last_week_r - season_first_week_r + 1) %>%
  left_join(co_weeks_all %>%
              group_by(taxon_capture) %>%
              summarise(co_weeks = sum(co_prev),
                        co_weeks_pos = sum(co_load),
                        # weeks spanned (first to last co-sampled week, on the re-originated axis)
                        co_span_weeks = if (any(co_prev)) max(week_r[co_prev]) - min(week_r[co_prev]) + 1 else 0,
                        co_span_weeks_pos = if (any(co_load)) max(week_r[co_load]) - min(week_r[co_load]) + 1 else 0,
                        .groups = "drop"),
            by = "taxon_capture") %>%
  mutate(include = n_adult >= min_n_stage & n_subadult >= min_n_stage,
         # one class per model part: prevalence (hu) uses weeks where both stages have
         # >= min_n_co swabs; load (mu) uses weeks where both have >= min_pos_co positives, which
         # is often much thinner (e.g. a species can be broad for prevalence, none for load)
         coverage_class_prev = classify_coverage(co_weeks, co_span_weeks),
         coverage_class_load = classify_coverage(co_weeks_pos, co_span_weeks_pos)) %>%
  arrange(desc(include), coverage_class_prev, coverage_class_load, desc(co_weeks))

write_csv(coverage_all, file.path(intermediates_dir, "01_season_coverage_all.csv"))

coverage_all

coverage_all %>% count(include, coverage_class_prev, coverage_class_load)

# species list for the all-species season model (02_season_all_species.qmd and the cluster
# script r-brms-contained/size_bd_season_all_modeling.R read this file, so the species, their
# order (= cluster array index) and their seasonal origins are defined in one place).
# alphabetical, so array indices do not change when thresholds move species between classes.
# copy to the cluster's data/ folder alongside the model data.
season_species_all = coverage_all %>%
  filter(include) %>%
  select(taxon_capture, origin_week, n_adult, n_subadult,
         coverage_class_prev, coverage_class_load, co_weeks, co_weeks_pos) %>%
  mutate(origin_doy = origin_week * 7 - 3,   # mid-week day of year, as in season_origin
         n = n_adult + n_subadult) %>%
  arrange(taxon_capture) %>%
  mutate(array_index = row_number() - 1)

write_csv(season_species_all, file.path(intermediates_dir, "01_season_species_all.csv"))

season_species_all
```

## Coverage plot
```{r}
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 14

# weekly swabs per species: adults above the axis, subadults below (mirrored), on the calendar
# week axis. shading marks co-sampled weeks (both stages >= min_n_co swabs); the dashed line is
# the seasonal origin (middle of the longest gap). the facet label gives the coverage
# class for prevalence / load.
cov_labels = coverage_all %>%
  # label: prevalence class / load class
  mutate(label = paste0(str_to_sentence(gsub("_", " ", taxon_capture)),
                        " (", coverage_class_prev, " / ", coverage_class_load,
                        if_else(include, "", ", excluded"), ")")) %>%
  select(taxon_capture, label)

p_coverage_all = weekly_all %>%
  filter(n > 0) %>%
  mutate(n_signed = if_else(life_stage_simple == "adult", n, -n)) %>%
  left_join(cov_labels, by = "taxon_capture") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = week)) +
  geom_rect(data = co_weeks_all %>% filter(co_prev) %>% left_join(cov_labels, by = "taxon_capture"),
            aes(xmin = week - 0.5, xmax = week + 0.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            fill = "grey85", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_col(aes(y = n_signed, fill = life_stage_simple), width = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(data = season_origin %>% left_join(cov_labels, by = "taxon_capture"),
             aes(xintercept = origin_week), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey30") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ label, scales = "free_y", ncol = 4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = stage_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = abs) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1, 52, by = 13), limits = c(0.5, 52.5)) +
  labs(x = "Week of year", y = "Swabs (adults up, subadults down)", fill = "Life stage",
       caption = "Grey: co-sampled weeks (prevalence rule). Dashed: seasonal origin (middle of the longest sampling gap).") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "italic"))
```

# Reading the screen

- A species is a good candidate for a Bayesian seasonal model if the interaction improves fit
  (clearly negative `delta_aic`), the fits converged, the contrast curve changes substantially
  across co-sampled weeks (not just a constant offset), and the separability reading is
  "seasonal" or "separable".
- A "not separable" reading means stage x season and stage-specific temperature sensitivity
  cannot be told apart with these data. A seasonal model could still describe *when* the stage
  difference is larger, but not *why* (date vs temperature). The stage x temp_anom estimate is
  the best available hint: near zero with a tight interval argues against temperature
  sensitivity.
- Check the design plots before trusting a strong interaction: a diagonal in the
  population x week plot means season and site are entangled.
